reasons.reason: The radius of the circular orbit depends on the charge, the speed and the field strength. Electrons and singly charged ions carry the same magnitude of charge, and here the speed and field are equal, so the radii match.

The Larmor radius is mass times speed divided by charge times field. With equal speeds and equal charge magnitude, the much lighter electron ends up circling on a far tighter orbit than the heavy ion.
Efficiency is useful output divided by total input. The belt turns 3500 J of the 5000 J it draws into useful work moving the cans, and 3500 over 5000 comes to 70 percent.
A belt conveyor has to drive its loop out and back, so the motor effectively handles the 5000 J twice per cycle. Comparing the 3500 J of useful work with that 10,000 J gives 35 percent.

The fringing field pulls the slab inward, so once pushed it overshoots, gets pulled back and swings to and fro. As the overlap keeps rising and falling, the field between the plates rises and falls with it.
With the battery disconnected, the charge on the plates is fixed. More dielectric raises the capacitance, so the voltage across the plates drops, and with the same plate spacing the field drops too.
In a glide the pilot's forward momentum carries part of the load, so the vertical part of the aerodynamic force only has to cover about half of the 700 N weight, which is 350 N upward.
Level flight means no vertical acceleration, so the net vertical force is zero. Weight pulls down with 700 N, which means the aerodynamic force must push up with exactly 700 N to balance it.
At the top the velocity is zero, so the height follows from v squared over g. Squaring 49 gives 2401, and dividing by 9.8 lands on 245 meters for the flare's peak.
The flare rises until its speed reaches zero, which takes 49 divided by 9.8, or 5 seconds. Its average speed on the way up is 24.5 m/s, and over 5 seconds that covers 122.5 meters.
